title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, October 2026 — the second regional Fed prices-paid read, published the same minute as the first
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey — the Philadelphia Fed's own MBOS landing page, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200) by the empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15 never-assessed initial research. Its 'next releases' block names the date and time verbatim: 'September 17, 2026 at 8:30 a.m.' and 'October 15, 2026 at 8:30 a.m.' Independently reproduced by the survey's own published cadence — MBOS releases on the THIRD THURSDAY of each month at 8:30 ET; September 2026's Thursdays are the 3rd, 10th and 17th, and October 2026's are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, so the third Thursdays are exactly the 17th and the 15th the page lists. Filed estimate on the same two counts as its sibling empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and a discovering lane may not self-confirm an event it found in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-08. It is filed for a measured reason rather than for completeness: this calendar tracks chicago-pmi and dallas-fed-mfg but carries ZERO Philadelphia Fed entries in any month, and MBOS is Empire State's direct methodological peer — the two are the only regional Fed manufacturing surveys that publish a prices-paid diffusion index at 8:30 ET, and on 2026-10-15 they publish it in the same minute. The pair is the point. On FRED's own series their prices-paid LEVELS correlate at r=0.908 over 302 months (r=0.934 since 2021), but in August 2026 they moved hard in opposite directions — Empire prices paid +6.3 to 58.6 (a 91st-percentile level over the full history) while Philly prices paid fell 13.0 to 40.9. That 19.3-point disagreement in one month's change sits at the 96th percentile of 301 months of Empire-vs-Philly divergence, against a median disagreement of 5.2 points. With gasoline at $4.071/gal for the week ending 2026-08-31 (+28.1% y/y, EIA primary) and a live question about energy pass-through into goods input costs, the two surveys are telling opposite stories about the thing the 10-28 FOMC is anchored to, and 2026-10-15 is the morning that adjudicates it. Tracking only one of the pair is the same selection bias the dallas-fed-mfg entry was filed to fix for the growth headline, transposed onto the prices line. Impact LOW and symbols empty for the same reasons as its sibling: no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys, none of the nine tracked names carries a Philadelphia-district manufacturing channel, and on 2026-10-15 this print shares 8:30 ET with retail sales (high) and PPI (medium), so its own tape effect is unattributable. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and whoever writes the canonical philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.json owns re-verifying the date.
